utility.notes: WestLight Energy's own announcement confirms PG&E's continued role: 'WestLight Energy customers see a new line item on their PG&E bill for WestLight Energy's service, along with a corresponding generation credit from PG&E for the energy supply PG&E previously provided.' PG&E is the underlying transmission/distribution/billing utility; WestLight Energy is a separate default generation supplier — see generation_supplier.

value: Building Official first verifies the submission is complete and code-compliant; a written correction notice is issued if deficiencies exist
Only one inspection is required and performed by the Building Division for eligible expedited-review systems
An inspection is scheduled within two business days of a request, with a two-hour inspection window
If the system fails the initial inspection, a subsequent inspection is authorized but need not follow the same scheduling requirements

timeline_days.notes: San Mateo Municipal Code Chapter 23.46 (Sections 23.46.040 and 23.46.070, directly read this session) states inspections are scheduled within 2 business days of a request, but no section found states an overall application-to-permit-issuance timeline distinct from that inspection-scheduling window — left null rather than substituting the inspection-scheduling figure for a permit-review timeline, which is a different concept.

other_conditions: Solar panel array may not exceed the maximum legal building height as defined by the City

eligibility_constraints.notes: Directly quoted from Municipal Code Section 23.46.020(g)'s definition of 'small residential rooftop solar energy system': 'no larger than 10 kilowatts alternating current nameplate rating of 30 kilowatts thermal' and 'installed on a single or duplex family dwelling.'
